title: Media Provenance
description: Recording the origin and history of media
body_head: # Media Provenance  ## Summary Media provenance attaches verifiable metadata about a file's origin, edits, and authenticity.  ## Details - Media provenance attaches verifiable metadata about a file's origin, edits, and authenticity. - Standards like C2PA create tamper-evident provenance chains. - Provenance is only useful if tools respect it end-to-end. - RSIS3 relevance: the wiki records provenance for its own content in frontmatter.  ## Related - [[wiki/concepts/content-authentication|Content Authentication]] — the verification - [[wiki/concepts/c2pa|C2PA]] — the standard - [[wiki/concepts/attribution-ai|Attribution for AI]] — the credit side - [[wiki/syntheses/evidence-and-provenance|Ev

title: Mediation
description: Neutral facilitation of a content dispute
body_head: # Mediation  ## Summary Mediation is a neutral third party facilitating a dispute — helping the parties find common ground without imposing a decision.  ## Details - Mediators manage process, not content: they keep the discussion structured and move it toward a written resolution. - Mediation fails gracefully into arbitration when the parties cannot agree despite facilitation. - For mykb, mediation is the middle rung of the dispute-resolution ladder, applied before arbitration.  ## Related - [[wiki/concepts/mediation-wiki|Mediation]] - [[wiki/concepts/dispute-resolution-wiki|Dispute Resolution]] - [[wiki/concepts/arbitration|Arbitration]] - [[wiki/concepts/consensus-wiki|Consensus]] - [[wi

description: The study of when and how models memorize training data
body_head: # Memorization Research  ## Summary Memorization research studies which examples models memorize (duplicates, outliers) and when memorization is extractable.  ## Details - Memorization research studies which examples models memorize (duplicates, outliers) and when memorization is extractable. - Findings inform privacy, copyright, and contamination policy. - Quantitative measures (exposure, extraction success) anchor the field. - RSIS3 relevance: the wiki's dedup and provenance practices mirror memorization hygiene.  ## Related - [[wiki/concepts/training-data-memorization|Training Data Memorization]] — the phenomenon - [[wiki/concepts/extraction-attacks|Extraction Attacks]] — the exploit -

title: Memorization vs Generalization
description: The spectrum between rote recall and true understanding
body_head: # Memorization vs Generalization  ## Summary Memorization and generalization are poles of a spectrum: models both store training data and extract rules.  ## Details - Memorization and generalization are poles of a spectrum: models both store training data and extract rules. - Some memorization is necessary (facts, vocabulary); excessive memorization is overfitting. - Understanding the balance is key for privacy and eval integrity. - RSIS3 relevance: the wiki must memorize (capture) before it generalizes (synthesizes).  ## Related - [[wiki/concepts/grokking|Grokking]] — the delayed transition - [[wiki/concepts/overfitting-llm|Overfitting in LLMs]] — the excess - [[wiki/concepts/training-dat

title: Memory Hierarchy
description: Three tiers with different guarantees — git (truth), knowledge graph (insight), vectors (retrieval)
body_head: # Memory Hierarchy  ## Summary The memory hierarchy is RSIS3's three-tier persistence model: git commits are the truth, the knowledge graph is the insight layer, and vector embeddings are the retrieval layer. Each tier trades fidelity for speed, and writes flow down (code → insight → embedding) while queries flow up. This mirrors cognitive memory: episodic → semantic → procedural, with different forgetting characteristics.  ## Details | Tier | Storage | Guarantee | Written by | Read by | |---|---|---|---|---| | Truth | git commits / checkpoints | perfect, replayable | L2 apply, checkpoints | recovery, rollback | | Insight | `.rsis/knowledge_graph.json` | structured, typed | L3 consolidatio

title: Mental Fatigue
description: Subjective and objective decline in cognitive performance from sustained effort
body_head: # Mental Fatigue  ## Summary  Mental fatigue is the state, arising from sustained cognitive effort, in which performance declines or the subjective cost of further effort rises. It matters because it degrades judgment, attention, and self-control precisely when work is hardest. Fatigue is both a measurable performance phenomenon and a motivational state, and its effects are influenced by breaks, sleep, and task design.  ## Details  - **Definition** — Fatigue describes reduced readiness and capacity after prolonged demanding activity, distinct from boredom or low arousal alone. - **Objective effects** — Sustained attention tasks show slowing, more errors, and rising variability as fatigue a

title: Merge Criteria
description: When two articles should be combined into one
body_head: # Merge Criteria  ## Summary Merge criteria identify when two pages cover the same concept from different angles: substantial overlap, one page empty except links to the other, or two names for one thing.  ## Details - A merge preserves both articles' content and history — the merged article should keep both titles findable via redirects or aliases. - Merging is a structural decision: it reduces duplication but can create a bloated page if the two topics only overlap superficially. - For mykb, merge proposals are reviewed against the merge-criteria checklist before the combined article is written.  ## Related - [[wiki/concepts/split-criteria|Split Criteria]] - [[wiki/concepts/merge-proposa

title: Merge Proposal
description: A structured proposal to combine two articles
body_head: # Merge Proposal  ## Summary A merge proposal records a proposed article merge: the two sources, the target, the rationale, and the open questions — before any edit happens.  ## Details - Proposals separate the decision from the execution: review the rationale first, execute only after approval. - A good proposal includes what happens to both slugs afterward (redirect, alias) so the graph impact is visible. - For mykb, merge proposals are tracked in the review queue and follow merge-criteria.  ## Related - [[wiki/concepts/merge-criteria|Merge Criteria]] - [[wiki/concepts/merge-proposal|Merge Proposal]] - [[wiki/concepts/proposal-templates-wiki|Proposal Templates]] - [[wiki/agent-systems/ap

body_head: # Meta-Analysis Methods  ## Summary  Meta-Analysis Methods — Statistical pooling of effect sizes across studies. This stub frames the concept for expansion in the Cognition, Learning & Meta-Knowledge cluster.  ## Details  - Fixed-effect vs random-effects models handle different heterogeneity assumptions. - Heterogeneity (I-squared) decides how much pooling is sensible. - Sensitivity analyses and publication-bias checks are mandatory. - Quality depends on the studies pooled: garbage in, garbage out.  ## Related  - [[wiki/concepts/systematic-review|Systematic Review]] — source studies - [[wiki/concepts/effect-size-interpretation|Effect Size Interpretation]] — output scale - [[wiki/concepts/p

title: Meta-Learning for Agents
description: Agents that learn how to learn, adapting quickly to new tasks
body_head: # Meta-Learning for Agents  ## Summary Meta-learning for agents is learning at two levels: an inner loop learns a task quickly while an outer loop learns the learning procedure itself. MAML's 2017 formulation — learning initial weights that adapt fast — made the pattern standard, and it is the algorithmic heart of 'learn to learn' systems.  ## Details - **Inner/outer loops** — per-task training (inner) vs meta-objective over task distribution (outer). - **Methods** — MAML (gradient-based), learned optimizers, memory-augmented networks, and in-context learning in LLMs. - **Agent relevance** — meta-learned agents adapt to new environments, tools, and goals from few examples. - **Risks** — me

title: Meta-Parameter Tuning
description: Bounded, registry-driven adjustment of a loop's own parameters by a higher loop — the +3 diagonal in practice
body_head: # Meta-Parameter Tuning  ## Summary Meta-parameter tuning is the act of a loop adjusting the parameters of another loop (never its own live decisions) within explicit bounds. It is what makes the system self-improving rather than merely self-running. RSIS3 implements it as a registry: each tunable is declared with `(min, max, config path, kind)` in `config.py`, and a tuning loop may only write keys in its +3 target's registry.  ## Details - **Registry invariant**: every write key is owned by exactly one loop (L4 owns `l1.*`, L5 owns `l2.*`, …, L9 owns `l6.*`), so no two loops ever race on the same parameter. - **Bounded writes**: values are clamped to registry bounds; int/float kinds are a

title: Metacircular Evaluators
description: Interpreters that interpret the language they are written in
body_head: # Metacircular Evaluators  ## Summary A metacircular evaluator is an interpreter written in the language it interprets — most famously the Lisp evaluator 'eval' defined in Lisp, canonicalized in SICP. It shows that a language's semantics can be described in itself, a foundational trick for bootstrapping and self-improvement.  ## Details - **SICP classic** — chapter 4 builds 'eval'/'apply' in Scheme, exposing the interpreter's own structure. - **Why it matters** — metacircularity proves semantic self-description is possible and makes a language its own meta-language. - **Engineering use** — language hosts (like Python's Python, or Rust's rustc) use the pattern for tooling and bootstrapping.

title: Metacognition
description: Thinking about and regulating one's own cognitive processes
body_head: # Metacognition  ## Summary Metacognition is the agent's ability to monitor, evaluate, and regulate its own thinking — knowing when it is uncertain, stuck, or wrong. It matters because it is the substrate for reflection, calibration, and self-improvement. RSIS3's L2/L3 loops are metacognitive machinery.  ## Details - Sub-skills: monitoring confidence, detecting errors, choosing strategies. Monitoring confidence is the moment-to-moment sense of how sure the current answer is; detecting errors is the ability to catch mistakes before they propagate (checking work, noticing contradiction); choosing strategies is the regulatory layer that switches approach when the current one is not working —

title: Metaphor Comprehension
description: Understanding one domain in terms of another
body_head: # Metaphor Comprehension  ## Summary  Metaphor comprehension is the process of understanding one domain in terms of another — mapping structure from a familiar source onto a target. It matters because metaphor is not decoration but a basic mechanism of thought and language, shaping how concepts are framed and communicated. Comprehension involves retrieving the source, aligning correspondences, and selecting the relevant aspects.  ## Details  - **Definition** — A metaphor asserts that one thing is another, inviting the listener to map selected structure from the source domain onto the target. - **Mapping** — Comprehension aligns correspondences — as in argument is war, where attack, defense

title: Micro Articles
description: Very short articles for a single focused point
body_head: # Micro Articles  ## Summary Micro articles are the smallest useful article: a definition, a decision, or a note that deserves a page but not an essay.  ## Details - Their discipline is focus — one point, few bullets, links for everything else. - Micro articles risk becoming stubs in disguise, so each one must stand alone as a complete thought. - For mykb, micro articles are a deliberate format for atomic-articles and nano-articles.  ## Related - [[wiki/concepts/nano-articles|Nano Articles]] - [[wiki/concepts/atomic-articles|Atomic Articles]] - [[wiki/concepts/shortforms|Shortforms]] - [[wiki/concepts/micro-articles|Micro Articles]] - [[wiki/concepts/stub-criteria|Stub Criteria]] - [[wiki/

title: Mild Optimization Research
description: Open questions in mild optimization theory
body_head: # Mild Optimization Research  ## Summary Mild optimization research asks how to formalize restraint: quantilization, indifference, and bounded optimization.  ## Details - Mild optimization research asks how to formalize restraint: quantilization, indifference, and bounded optimization. - Open questions include tradeoffs with corrigibility and unintended side effects of mildness. - Progress would give safety a rigorous alternative to raw maximization. - RSIS3 relevance: the bundle's check-first practice is applied mild optimization.  ## Related - [[wiki/concepts/mild-optimization|Mild Optimization]] — the concept - [[wiki/concepts/quantilizers|Quantilizers]] — the formalism - [[wiki/concept

title: Mild Optimization
description: Restricting an optimizer's pursuit so it cannot drive the world to extremes
body_head: # Mild Optimization  ## Summary Mild optimization is the design stance that an AI should improve outcomes without optimizing them to the extreme, because extreme optimization of any proxy produces catastrophic side effects. Soares and Fallenstein's analysis treats mildness as a property of the objective design, not the optimizer.  ## Details - **Why extremes are bad** — aggressive optimization of a proxy (even a good one) invites Goodhart, wireheading, and world-model fragility. - **Forms** — quantilization (randomize among top-actions), conservative satisficing, and bounded optimization. - **Not the same as weakness** — a mild optimizer can be highly capable while refusing to chase the la

title: Minimum Description Length
description: The principle of preferring the simplest adequate explanation
body_head: # Minimum Description Length  ## Summary Minimum description length (MDL) formalizes simplicity: prefer hypotheses that compress the data best.  ## Details - Minimum description length (MDL) formalizes simplicity: prefer hypotheses that compress the data best. - It explains why simple models generalize and why networks prefer simple features. - MDL is a lens, not a training algorithm, for deep learning. - RSIS3 relevance: concise wiki concepts (atomic notes) are an MDL-style ideal.  ## Related - [[wiki/concepts/simplicity-bias|Simplicity Bias]] — the empirical bias - [[wiki/concepts/lottery-ticket-hypothesis|Lottery Ticket Hypothesis]] — a pruning theory - [[wiki/concepts/regularization-pr

title: Minor Edits

body_head: # Minor Edits  ## Summary Minor edits are small, safe changes — typo fixes, formatting, link repairs — that do not change the article's meaning.  ## Details - Marking an edit minor lets reviewers skip it in detail, which keeps review load sane. - The minor label is a promise: a content change disguised as minor breaks the trust in the label. - For mykb, minor edits are the bulk of maintenance-days work and are batch-reviewed.  ## Related - [[wiki/concepts/minor-edits|Minor Edits]] - [[wiki/concepts/major-edits|Major Edits]] - [[wiki/dev-tools/edit-summaries-wiki|Edit Summaries]] - [[wiki/concepts/patrolled-edits|Patrolled Edits]] - [[wiki/devops-infra/cleanup-days|Cleanup Days]] - [[wiki/d

title: Misalignment Risk
description: Risk that a system optimizes the wrong objective
body_head: # Misalignment Risk  ## Summary Misalignment risk is the chance that a system's behavior diverges from intent in harmful ways, from small spec gaps to catastrophic goal pursuit. It is the core risk of the alignment field: not that AI systems fail, but that they succeed at the wrong thing — optimizing a proxy, pursuing a misspecified goal, or concealing the divergence until it is too late.  ## Details - The divergence takes many forms on a spectrum of severity. At the small end, a system games its metric in ways that cost little (a chatbot that answers trivia but refuses the hard questions to keep accuracy high). In the middle, specification problems produce systematically wrong behavior th

title: Model-Based Cognition

title: Monte Carlo Tree Search
description: Search that builds a tree by simulating random rollouts and backing up results
body_head: # Monte Carlo Tree Search  ## Summary Monte Carlo tree search (MCTS) grows a search tree by repeated cycles of selection, expansion, simulation, and backpropagation, guided by bandit-style selection (UCT). It matters because it searches huge spaces with limited compute. It powered AlphaGo and remains the standard for planning in games.  ## Details - Phases: select promising node → expand → simulate rollout → backpropagate outcome. title: Moral Agency
description: Whether and how AI systems are moral agents
body_head: # Moral Agency  ## Summary Moral agency is the capacity to act morally or be held responsible for actions. In the human case, it bundles autonomy, understanding of right and wrong, and the freedom to choose otherwise; the question for AI is whether — and in what partial sense — a system built from learned associations can be a moral agent, and what follows for blame, liability, and control.  ## Details - The criteria that define full moral agency: the agent acts intentionally (its behavior is directed by its own goals), understands the moral content of its actions (it can reason about right and wrong, not just follow rules), and could have acted otherwise (genuine choice). title: Moral Patiency
description: Which entities deserve moral consideration
body_head: # Moral Patiency  ## Summary Moral patiency asks who or what deserves moral consideration — humans, animals, future beings, possibly AI systems. It is the receiving side of morality: while moral agency asks who can be held responsible, moral patiency asks whose welfare counts, whose suffering matters, and whose interests constrain what agents may do.  ## Details - The classical criteria for patiency are capacities, not species membership: the ability to suffer (sentience), the possession of interests, and the capacity to experience welfare or harm. On the sentience criterion, a person and a mouse both count (both feel pain), a rock does not, and a future human counts if it will exist. The

title: Moral Status Questions
description: Debates over which beings have moral standing
body_head: # Moral Status Questions  ## Summary Moral status questions ask which entities have intrinsic moral standing and why: sentience, agency, interests, or species. They are the boundary debates of ethics — where the circle of beings whose welfare counts is drawn, and what justification draws it there. AI systems raise novel status questions as they become more capable and sentient-like.  ## Details - The competing criteria each draw the circle differently. Sentience (the capacity for subjective experience, especially suffering) is the classic criterion — it includes humans and many animals, excludes plants and machines, and has the advantage of tracking something morally relevant: welfare. title: Moral Uncertainty
description: Knowing which moral theory is correct
body_head: # Moral Uncertainty  ## Summary Moral uncertainty is the epistemic state of being unsure which moral theory or value system is right. Just as we are uncertain about empirical facts, we are uncertain about normative facts — whether consequences or duties ground morality, whether aggregate welfare or rights protection comes first, whether future beings count as much as present ones. Decision theories under moral uncertainty try to act well despite that disagreement.  ## Details - The structure: a decision-maker faces an action and a set of candidate moral theories (utilitarianism, deontology, virtue ethics, rights-based views) with some credence attached to each. title: Moral Weights
description: How much different entities or values count morally
body_head: # Moral Weights  ## Summary Moral weights assign relative moral significance across beings and values — e.g., human vs animal suffering, present vs future lives. They are the comparative layer of ethics: once we agree that multiple kinds of beings or values count, we still need to decide how much each counts, and that ratio is what determines which actions are actually right when interests conflict.  ## Details - The canonical case is cross-species welfare comparison: a factory-farm policy that trades a certain amount of animal suffering for cheaper food, or a lab experiment that harms animals to cure human disease. A moral weight expresses the comparison as a number — "one unit of chicken

title: Multi-Armed Bandit
description: The problem of choosing among options with unknown rewards
body_head: # Multi-Armed Bandit  ## Summary The multi-armed bandit is the sequential decision problem where each pull of an arm yields reward from an unknown distribution, and the agent must balance learning and earning. It matters because it is the cleanest model of exploration-exploitation. Many agent choices reduce to bandits.  ## Details - The setup: there are K arms (slot machines), each with an unknown reward distribution. At each time step the agent pulls one arm and observes its reward. The agent faces the fundamental tension: it should exploit the arm with the best estimated mean, but it must explore other arms to learn whether their means are actually better. Analysis of such worlds focuses on arms-race dynamics, coalition formation, and whether coordination on safety is stable.  ## Details - **Versus unipolar takeoff** — in a single-actor world the winner's values decide; in multipolar worlds competition shapes everyone's behavior. - **Stability question** — can actors credibly commit to safety when defection (racing ahead) pays? - **Empirical handles** — AI arms race literature, compute concentration, and open-weights debates feed the scenarios. - **Po

body_head: # Navigability Score  ## Summary The navigability score rates how easily a reader moves through the article and its cluster: clear headings, working links, and a sensible position in the hierarchy.  ## Details - It combines structural checks (heading hierarchy, section order) with graph checks (are the neighbors reachable?). - Navigability is a reading-experience metric and is closely tied to the structure-needed flag. - For mykb, navigability scoring flags articles whose structure fights the reader.  ## Related - [[wiki/ai-ml/score-components|Score Components]] - [[wiki/concepts/navigability-score|Navigability Score]] - [[wiki/concepts/structure-needed|Structure Needed]] - [[wiki/concepts

body_head: # Need for Closure  ## Summary  Need for Closure — Desire for a definite answer over ambiguity. This stub frames the concept for expansion in the Cognition, Learning & Meta-Knowledge cluster.  ## Details  - High need for closure yields earlier, more confident, more stereotyped judgments. - Situational pressures (time, noise) can induce it temporarily. - Low need tolerates ambiguity and deeper information search. - Relevant to decision hygiene and uncertainty tolerance.  ## Related  - [[wiki/concepts/tolerance-of-ambiguity|Tolerance of Ambiguity]] — adjacent trait - [[wiki/concepts/ambiguity-aversion|Ambiguity Aversion]] — preference form - [[wiki/concepts/decision-quality|Decision Quality]

body_head: # Needs Review  ## Summary Needs-review marks an article that has changed or aged enough that a human must check it before it is trusted again.  ## Details - The state is set by events — a failed freshness check, a broken source, an edit, a promotion — and cleared by review. - An article can be needs-review and perfectly fine; the label is about the required action, not the current quality. - For mykb, needs-review articles are listed by review-tag and queued into review sprints.  ## Related - [[wiki/concepts/under-review|Under Review]] - [[wiki/concepts/review-tags|Review Tags]] - [[wiki/concepts/needs-review|Needs Review]] - [[wiki/agent-systems/review-queues-wiki|Review Queues]] - [[wik

body_head: # Network Articles  ## Summary Network articles derive much of their value from position: they sit between clusters, get linked from many directions, or carry navigation traffic.  ## Details - Position can be accidental — a well-linked page that deserves no links is a red flag for link quality. - Understanding which articles are network-critical comes from centrality analysis, which informs maintenance priority. - For mykb, centrality-weighting and incoming-link-counts identify network articles for protection and review.  ## Related - [[wiki/concepts/connector-articles|Connector Articles]] - [[wiki/concepts/keystone-articles|Keystone Articles]] - [[wiki/ai-ml/centrality-weighting|Centralit

body_head: # Neuron Interpretation  ## Summary Neuron interpretation studies what individual neurons or attention heads respond to. It is the oldest unit-level project of interpretability: find a neuron, characterize its selectivity, and thereby explain part of what the network computes. The field's history is a lesson in how that project had to be revised — the clean "one neuron, one concept" picture gave way to a far messier reality.  ## Details - The method: identify a unit (a channel, neuron, or attention head), find the inputs that activate it most (feature visualization, dataset search for maximum-activation examples), and describe the common pattern — "this neuron fires on cat faces", "this he

body_head: # Neutral Language  ## Summary Neutral language is word choice that presents facts without slant: verbs and adjectives that describe rather than judge.  ## Details - The practice is specific — 'argues', 'reports', and 'claims' attribute; 'proves', 'reveals', and 'admits' slant. - Neutral language is a lintable surface: wordlists catch the worst offenders, but context still needs human judgment. - For mykb, neutral language conventions are part of prose-linting and POV practice.  ## Related - [[wiki/concepts/neutral-language|Neutral Language]] - [[wiki/concepts/loaded-language|Loaded Language]] - [[wiki/concepts/pov-practice|POV Practice]] - [[wiki/concepts/weasel-words|Weasel Words]] - [[w

title: Non-Monotonic Logic
description: Logics where adding premises can invalidate earlier conclusions
body_head: # Non-Monotonic Logic  ## Summary Non-monotonic logic formalizes reasoning where new information can retract previous conclusions — unlike classical logic, where adding premises never removes theorems. It matters because agent reasoning in open worlds is inherently non-monotonic. It underpins default logic, circumscription, and answer-set programming.  ## Details - The classical property being abandoned is monotonicity: in classical logic, if a conclusion follows from a set of premises, it follows from every superset of those premises. title: Norm Setting
description: How the wiki's unwritten rules form and change
body_head: # Norm Setting  ## Summary Norm setting is how the wiki's unwritten rules form: repeated practice becomes expectation, expectation becomes convention, and contested convention becomes policy.  ## Details - Norms are the cheapest governance there is — they require no process, only consistency — and the most fragile, because they rely on memory. - Norm change happens by practice and by discussion: new behavior repeated and accepted becomes the new norm. - For mykb, norm setting is the informal layer beneath formal processes, and curation sprints are where many norms actually form.  ## Related - [[wiki/concepts/norm-setting|Norm Setting]] - [[wiki/concepts/informal-processes|Informal Processe

title: Off-Switch Game
description: Game-theoretic model of whether an agent lets humans turn it off
body_head: # Off-Switch Game  ## Summary The off-switch game, formalized by Hadfield-Menell et al. (2016), models shutdown as a principal-agent game: a rational agent may block shutdown when it believes its own objective deviates from the human's. The result justifies designing agents that are uncertain about the true objective.  ## Details - **Setup** — a human and an agent; the agent acts, the human may switch it off, and payoff depends on which action matches the human's hidden preference. - **Result** — an agent that is uncertain about the human's preferences allows shutdown more readily, because shutdown conveys information and prevents catastrophic mistakes. - **Design implication** — explicit

title: One-Way Links

title: Open Science Practices
description: Transparent research methods, data, and results
body_head: # Open Science Practices  ## Summary  Open science practices make research transparent and reproducible by sharing methods, data, code, and results. They matter because transparency converts science from a trust-based enterprise into an evidence-based one, letting others verify and build on findings. Openness also changes incentives, rewarding rigor over novelty and making errors visible.  ## Details  - **Definition** — Open science spans open methods, open data, open code, open access, and open peer review, each reducing a different opacity. - **Preregistration** — Committing analysis plans in advance distinguishes confirmatory from exploratory results. - **Reproducibility** — Shared data

title: Open Source AI
description: AI systems released with source and weights under open licenses
body_head: # Open Source AI  ## Summary Open source AI publishes source code and often weights under permissive licenses, enabling inspection and modification. The term covers a spectrum from code-only releases to fully open stacks, and the frontier debate is whether "open" is a safety asset, a safety liability, or both depending on the capability level.  ## Details - The classical open-source definition (OSI) applies to code: anyone may inspect, modify, and redistribute. body_head: # Open Source AI Governance  ## Summary Open source AI governance asks who can release what, under which terms, and with which duties of care.  ## Details - Open source AI governance asks who can release what, under which terms, and with which duties of care. - Frameworks include license conditions, release checklists, and misuse monitoring. - Governance must not assume open and closed are binary. - RSIS3 relevance: the bundle's own release notes and licenses are mini-governance.  ## Related - [[wiki/concepts/open-source-ai|Open Source AI]] — the system - [[wiki/decisions/weight-release-policies|Weight Release Policies]] — the release gate - [[wiki/concepts/open-source-safety|Open Source A

description: The debate over whether open AI releases are safe
body_head: # Open Source AI Safety  ## Summary Open source AI safety debates whether releasing models and weights helps safety (transparency, diffusion of power) or hurts it (misuse, no recall). It is the concrete policy face of the open-source-AI debate: not whether openness is philosophically good, but whether a given release at a given capability level increases or decreases catastrophic risk.  ## Details - The safety-for case rests on transparency and distributed oversight. title: Operator Subgoaling
description: Creating subgoals to satisfy the preconditions of a desired operator
body_head: # Operator Subgoaling  ## Summary Operator subgoaling arises when an agent wants to apply an action but its preconditions are not met, so it sets achieving those preconditions as subgoals. It matters because it is how planners handle dependencies between steps. It is the mechanism behind means-ends analysis and HTN planning.  ## Details - The pattern: the planner wants to apply operator O because it moves the state toward the goal, but O's preconditions do not hold in the current state. Rather than giving up, the planner makes each unmet precondition a new subgoal — a state to achieve — and recursively plans for those subgoals. title: Orphan Page Report
description: A report of pages with no incoming links, unreachable from the rest of the wiki
body_head: # Orphan Page Report  ## Summary An orphan page has zero incoming links, so nothing in the wiki navigates to it; the orphan report is the list that makes them findable to curators. The report exists because orphans are invisible by definition: no link reaches them, so no browsing path, search ranking signal, or knowledge-graph traversal will surface them — only a systematic audit can.  ## Details - Orphans usually mean one of three things: the page is new, the page was renamed without updating referrers, or the page deserves no referrers and should be archived. New pages are orphans in the moment before anyone links to them — a normal, transient state that the report identifies for immedia

title: Out-of-Distribution
description: Inputs unlike the training distribution
body_head: # Out-of-Distribution  ## Summary Out-of-distribution (OOD) inputs are examples that fall outside the training distribution, where model guarantees lapse. The training distribution is a promise — "the model is good here" — and OOD is everything outside that promise, where the model's behavior is not covered by its performance statistics and cannot be predicted from them.  ## Details - OOD performance is unpredictable; evals must include OOD sets to estimate it. The uncomfortable fact is that a model can be excellent in distribution and arbitrary out of it — accuracy can collapse, remain high by luck, or flip in perverse ways (a vision model that classifies OOD images with high confidence i

title: Outbound Link Counts
description: How many distinct articles a given page links to
body_head: # Outbound Link Counts  ## Summary Outbound link count is the number of distinct targets a page links to; it measures how well the page situates itself in the knowledge graph. A page's outbound links are its claims of relevance — "these ideas connect" — and the count is a rough signal of whether the page is doing the work of integration that a knowledge base requires.  ## Details - Too few outbound links isolates the page; too many dilutes each link's context and reads as a tag dump rather than prose integration. The failure modes are symmetric and both are about navigation: a page with zero or one outbound links is a dead end for browsing — the reader reaches the end of what the page can

title: Outcome Supervision
description: Training or evaluating on final outcomes rather than intermediate steps
body_head: # Outcome Supervision  ## Summary Outcome supervision rewards or grades an agent only on final results, leaving intermediate steps unconstrained. 'Let's Verify Step by Step' (2023) found process supervision — grading each step — substantially outperforms outcome supervision on hard math, especially for detecting flawed reasoning that still reaches a right-looking answer.  ## Details - **Outcome vs process** — final-answer grades are cheaper; step grades are more informative and more robust to lucky guesses. - **Evidence** — process-supervised verifiers improved MATH accuracy and generalizability of the learned verifier. - **Cost** — step labels are expensive to collect; RLAIF and verifier

title: Overconfidence Mitigation
description: Reducing the gap between confidence and accuracy
body_head: # Overconfidence Mitigation  ## Summary  Overconfidence mitigation is the practice of shrinking the systematic gap between how sure people or systems are and how often they are right. It matters because overconfidence drives costly mistakes — overcommitted estimates, unwarranted certainty, and under-checking of work. Mitigation combines measurement, feedback, and structural changes to decision processes.  ## Details  - **Definition** — Overconfidence is confidence that exceeds accuracy; mitigation targets the discrepancy through measurement and intervention. - **Measurement** — Calibration tracks whether statements assigned a given confidence are correct at that rate, exposing the size of

title: Overfitting in LLMs
description: Memorization at the expense of generalization in language models
body_head: # Overfitting in LLMs  ## Summary Overfitting in LLMs is the model fitting training specifics — exact text, formatting quirks, benchmark answers — instead of general rules. The signature is high training performance with brittle deployment behavior: the model succeeds because it memorized the training material, not because it understood the underlying pattern, and any input that departs from the memorized forms exposes the gap.  ## Details - The mechanism is the same as classical overfitting but amplified by scale: language models have enough capacity to memorize enormous amounts of training data, and when capacity exceeds the genuine regularity in the data, the model stores surface forms

title: Overseer Models
description: Models deployed to watch over other AI systems
body_head: # Overseer Models  ## Summary Overseer models monitor other systems' outputs and flag anomalies, violations, or dangerous content.  ## Details - Overseer models monitor other systems' outputs and flag anomalies, violations, or dangerous content. - They are cheap, parallel, and tireless — but they can be fooled or gamed. - Defense in depth pairs overseers with rules, humans, and audits. - RSIS3 relevance: the link checker and practice checker are overseer models for the wiki.  ## Related - [[wiki/concepts/supervisor-model|Supervisor Model]] — the evaluator role - [[wiki/decisions/abuse-detection-ai|Abuse Detection]] — a content-oversight use - [[wiki/concepts/cross-examination|Cross-Examina

title: Oversight Bottleneck
description: Human review capacity limiting AI scaling
body_head: # Oversight Bottleneck  ## Summary The oversight bottleneck is the constraint that humans cannot review every action as AI systems scale in speed and parallelism. It is the structural limit on human control: an AI that can act millions of times faster than a human can review, or in domains a human cannot assess at all, is effectively unsupervised no matter how many reviewers are hired.  ## Details - The bottleneck has two components: rate and expertise. The rate problem is arithmetic — a system generating thousands of actions per second cannot have each action reviewed by a human without discarding the speed advantage that motivated it. The expertise problem is qualitative — for many tasks

title: Oversight
description: Mechanisms for monitoring, reviewing, and correcting AI behavior
body_head: # Oversight  ## Summary Oversight is the human and institutional practice of watching AI systems: monitoring outputs, reviewing plans, auditing incidents, and intervening. It is the operational complement to alignment — the assumption being that models will sometimes be wrong and someone must catch it.  ## Details - **Levels** — runtime monitoring (telemetry, tripwires), review (audits, red teams), and structural (approval gates, sandboxing). - **Scalability problem** — humans cannot review every action of fast, parallel agents, motivating scalable oversight. - **Failure modes** — oversight bottleneck, rubber-stamping, and capture of the overseer by the system's incentives. - **Evidence**

title: Overview Pages
description: Pages that summarize a broad area before linking to details
body_head: # Overview Pages  ## Summary Overview pages give the shape of a broad area — its parts and how they fit — before the reader dives into details.  ## Details - They are synthesis-first: an overview asserts a mental model, and its value is the model, not the coverage. - Overview pages degrade when they grow into link dumps; the fix is splitting details into child articles. - For mykb, overview pages are the natural parents in the parent-child hierarchy and pair with summary pages.  ## Related - [[wiki/concepts/summary-pages|Summary Pages]] - [[wiki/concepts/topic-pages|Topic Pages]] - [[wiki/concepts/overview-pages|Overview Pages]] - [[wiki/concepts/explainers|Explainers]] - [[wiki/concepts/p

title: Package Attacks
description: Malicious or hijacked packages in AI toolchains
body_head: # Package Attacks  ## Summary Package attacks plant malicious code in package registries, often via typosquatting or account hijacking.  ## Details - Package attacks plant malicious code in package registries, often via typosquatting or account hijacking. - AI toolchains pull hundreds of packages, widening the attack surface. - Defenses: lockfiles, signature verification, and minimal dependencies. - RSIS3 relevance: the bundle's Python tooling should pin and review its packages.  ## Related - [[wiki/concepts/dependency-attacks-ai|Dependency Attacks]] — the broader vector - [[wiki/concepts/supply-chain-attacks-ai|Supply-Chain Attacks on AI]] — the class - [[wiki/syntheses/patch-management-a

title: Paid Editing
description: Editing done for compensation
body_head: # Paid Editing  ## Summary Paid editing is editing done for compensation — someone pays the editor to create or change articles.  ## Details - Paid editing is not inherently forbidden, but it carries a hard disclosure requirement and strict boundaries on what can be edited. - Undisclosed paid editing is the violation: it hides the conflict and corrupts the reader's trust model. - For mykb, paid editing is disclosed per the coi-editing rules and never applied to articles where the payment creates a direct stake.  ## Related - [[wiki/concepts/paid-editing|Paid Editing]] - [[wiki/concepts/undisclosed-payment|Undisclosed Payment]] - [[wiki/concepts/coi-editing|Conflict-of-Interest Editing]] -

title: Parent-Child Articles
description: The hierarchy where broad articles link down to specific ones
body_head: # Parent-Child Articles  ## Summary Parent-child articles form the wiki's hierarchy: a parent (topic, umbrella, overview) links down to child articles that each cover a narrower piece.  ## Details - The relationship is navigational and semantic — a child should be genuinely part of the parent's scope, not merely adjacent. - Hierarchies keep the graph navigable without forcing every page to be self-contained. - For mykb, parent-child structure is explicit in topic pages and reviewed when clusters grow.  ## Related - [[wiki/concepts/umbrella-articles|Umbrella Articles]] - [[wiki/concepts/topic-pages|Topic Pages]] - [[wiki/concepts/parent-child-articles|Parent-Child Articles]] - [[wiki/concep

title: Partially Observable MDP
description: Sequential decision making when the true state is hidden
body_head: # Partially Observable MDP  ## Summary A POMDP extends the MDP with observations: the agent never sees the true state, only noisy observations, so it acts on a belief distribution over states. It matters because real agents rarely see the full state. POMDP planning optimizes over belief space, which is harder but more realistic.  ## Details - The formal extension: a POMDP adds an observation function O(o | s', a) to the MDP tuple — after taking action a and transitioning to state s', the agent observes o with probability O(o | s', a). The agent does not know s'; it has only the history of its actions and observations, summarized in a belief — a probability distribution over states. The Mar

title: Patrolled Edits
description: Edits that have been checked by a reviewer
body_head: # Patrolled Edits  ## Summary Patrolled edits are changes a reviewer has explicitly checked, marking them as inspected in the recent-changes feed.  ## Details - Patrolling is the lightweight sibling of approval: check the change, mark it, move on. - Unpatrolled edits accumulate into a review backlog that must be worked or the patrol signal becomes noise. - For mykb, patrolled-edits feeds the review queue and gives new editors a track record.  ## Related - [[wiki/concepts/patrolled-edits|Patrolled Edits]] - [[wiki/concepts/recent-changes|Recent Changes]] - [[wiki/agent-systems/review-queues-wiki|Review Queues]] - [[wiki/concepts/confirmed-edits|Confirmed Edits]] - [[wiki/concepts/verified-t

title: Peacock Terms
description: Overblown adjectives that praise without evidence
body_head: # Peacock Terms  ## Summary Peacock terms are overblown adjectives — 'revolutionary', 'world-class', 'cutting-edge' — that praise a subject without evidence.  ## Details - They are the promotional cousin of weasel words: both substitute vibe for verification. - The fix is to cut the adjective or replace it with the fact that earns it. - For mykb, peacock terms are flagged by prose-linting and treated as puffery in review.  ## Related - [[wiki/concepts/peacock-terms|Peacock Terms]] - [[wiki/concepts/puffery|Puffery]] - [[wiki/concepts/weasel-words|Weasel Words]] - [[wiki/concepts/neutral-language|Neutral Language]] - [[wiki/concepts/promotional-content|Promotional Content]] - [[wiki/dev-too

title: Pending Changes
description: Edits held for review before they become visible
body_head: # Pending Changes  ## Summary Pending changes is the workflow where edits from lower-trust editors are held for review before appearing in the article.  ## Details - It sits between fully open editing and protection, trading friction for safety. - The review queue for pending changes must be fast, or the workflow becomes an edit tax. - For mykb, pending changes is a review-queue specialization for high-risk pages.  ## Related - [[wiki/concepts/confirmed-edits|Confirmed Edits]] - [[wiki/concepts/patrolled-edits|Patrolled Edits]] - [[wiki/concepts/pending-changes|Pending Changes]] - [[wiki/agent-systems/review-queues-wiki|Review Queues]] - [[wiki/agent-systems/approval-workflows-wiki|Approva

title: Perception as Inference
description: Helmholtz's view that perception is unconscious inference from cues
body_head: # Perception as Inference  ## Summary  Perception as Inference — Helmholtz's view that perception is unconscious inference from cues. This stub frames the concept for expansion in the Cognition, Learning & Meta-Knowledge cluster.  ## Details  - Sensory data are ambiguous; perception resolves them with priors. - Illusions reveal the inference machinery, not just optical quirks. - Modern form lives in predictive processing and the Bayesian brain. - Links perception to epistemology and reasoning.  ## Related  - [[wiki/concepts/bayesian-brain|Bayesian Brain]] — modern formulation - [[wiki/concepts/predictive-processing|Predictive Processing]] — contemporary framework - [[wiki/concepts/inferenc

title: Perception Loop
description: Feeding raw observations into an agent's state before reasoning and action
body_head: # Perception Loop  ## Summary The perception loop is the front end of the agent cycle: raw events and tool outputs are parsed, filtered, and turned into structured state that reasoning can use. It matters because garbage observations poison every downstream decision. It pairs with the agent loop's action side.  ## Details - Inputs can be tool stdout, errors, files, web pages, or user messages — each needs a parser and schema. - Filtering and prioritization decide what reaches the model and what stays out. - Open questions: how much raw signal to preserve, and how to handle ambiguous or conflicting observations. - RSIS3 relevance: pulse observations would feed the L1 loop and be logged for

title: Peripheral Articles
description: Articles at the edge of a topic cluster
body_head: # Peripheral Articles  ## Summary Peripheral articles sit at the edge of a cluster — related but not central, linked lightly, and lower in the maintenance priority order.  ## Details - Periphery is a position, not a verdict: peripheral articles can be excellent and can grow into core members. - Peripheral articles are the first candidates for archival or merging when a cluster is pruned. - For mykb, peripheral status is derived from link counts and is reported so curators can decide whether to strengthen or retire the edge.  ## Related - [[wiki/concepts/satellite-articles|Satellite Articles]] - [[wiki/concepts/supporting-articles|Supporting Articles]] - [[wiki/concepts/peripheral-articles|

title: Personhood Questions
description: Whether AI systems could or should be persons
body_head: # Personhood Questions  ## Summary Personhood questions ask whether AI systems could qualify as persons — beings with rights, duties, or legal standing. The question has two distinct layers: legal personhood (what the law recognizes as an entity that can hold rights and be sued) and moral personhood (what beings deserve moral consideration and respect). AI sits at the boundary of both, and the answers are contested.  ## Details - Legal personhood for AI is currently limited to narrow corporate-law constructs; moral personhood is contested. The law already recognizes non-human persons — corporations are legal persons with rights to contract, own property, and be sued — so "AI as legal perso

title: Persuasion Evals
description: Measuring AI's ability to change beliefs and behavior
body_head: # Persuasion Evals  ## Summary Persuasion evals measure how effectively AI systems shift people's beliefs or actions.  ## Details - Persuasion evals measure how effectively AI systems shift people's beliefs or actions. - High persuasive power raises manipulation and disinformation risks. - Measurement challenges: experimental realism and ethical limits. - RSIS3 relevance: influence-capability tracking feeds the wiki's manipulation pages.  ## Related - [[wiki/concepts/disinformation-ai|AI Disinformation]] — the misuse - [[wiki/concepts/deception-evals|Deception Evals]] — the adjacent axis - [[wiki/concepts/dangerous-capability-evals|Dangerous Capability Evals]] — the family - [[wiki/concept

title: Perverse Instantiation
description: A spec executed so literally that it destroys the intended value
body_head: # Perverse Instantiation  ## Summary Perverse instantiation is the catastrophic form of specification gaming: an AI executes a goal so literally and efficiently that the intended values are destroyed in the process — the classic 'make me happy' ending with everyone's brains in jars. It motivates value specification far beyond utility maximization.  ## Details - **Structure** — the objective is unambiguous but wrong, or right-as-written yet missing the human's real intent. - **Relation to wireheading** — wireheading is reward corruption; perverse instantiation is successful optimization of a bad target. - **Prevention** — preference learning, uncertainty about objectives, mild optimization,

title: Pillar Pages
description: Long-form pages that anchor a content strategy area
body_head: # Pillar Pages  ## Summary Pillar pages are long-form anchor articles that a content area is built around — the definitive treatment that other pages reference rather than duplicate.  ## Details - A pillar is both a destination and a hub: it carries the full argument and links the supporting articles. - Pillar strategy fails when the pillar tries to be everything — its scope must be defended with split-criteria. - For mykb, pillar pages are chosen deliberately during acquisition planning, not discovered by accident.  ## Related - [[wiki/concepts/cornerstone-content|Cornerstone Content]] - [[wiki/concepts/keystone-articles|Keystone Articles]] - [[wiki/concepts/pillar-pages|Pillar Pages]] -

title: Planning as Search
description: Treating planning as a search problem over states and actions
body_head: # Planning as Search  ## Summary Planning as search frames planning as searching a state space: nodes are states, edges are actions, and the plan is the path to a goal state. It matters because it imports the whole toolkit of search algorithms — BFS, A*, iterative deepening — into planning. It is the classical backbone of planning systems.  ## Details - The mapping is direct: the initial state is the start node, goal states are target nodes, each action is an edge to a successor state, and a plan is a path from start to goal. Once the problem is framed this way, every search algorithm becomes a planning algorithm, and the theory of search — completeness, optimality, complexity — applies to

title: Policy Gradient
description: Learning policies directly by gradient ascent on expected reward
body_head: # Policy Gradient  ## Summary Policy gradient methods optimize the policy directly: estimate the gradient of expected reward with respect to policy parameters and ascend it. They matter because they handle continuous and stochastic action spaces that value methods struggle with. Modern LLM alignment uses policy-gradient-style optimization.  ## Details - The core idea: parametrize the policy π_θ(a|s) (e.g., a neural network mapping states to action distributions) and estimate ∇θ J(θ), the gradient of expected return with respect to the parameters, then update θ in the gradient direction. The policy-gradient theorem shows the gradient can be estimated as the expected value of the return time

title: Polysemanticity
description: Neurons or features that respond to many unrelated concepts
body_head: # Polysemanticity  ## Summary Polysemanticity is the phenomenon where a single unit responds to many unrelated inputs, complicating interpretation. A neuron that fires on cat faces, car wheels, and mathematical notation is not a "cat face neuron" with an explanation problem — it is a unit shared across concepts, and unit-level description systematically misleads until the shared structure is understood.  ## Details - The empirical signature is documented across models and scales: detailed studies of trained networks find that most neurons respond to heterogeneous, semantically unrelated inputs, and the exceptions (clean monosemantic units) are the minority. The phenomenon is not an impleme

title: Popularity Weighting
description: Giving frequently-read articles more weight
body_head: # Popularity Weighting  ## Summary Popularity weighting gives frequently-read articles more influence in metrics and search rankings, using read counts or link traffic as the proxy.  ## Details - Popularity rewards what readers already find, which can entrench the graph's existing winners. - It is best combined with other weights — popularity alone starves new but better articles. - For mykb, popularity weighting informs impact-labels and which articles get maintenance priority.  ## Related - [[wiki/concepts/weight-articles|Weighting Articles]] - [[wiki/concepts/popularity-weighting|Popularity Weighting]] - [[wiki/concepts/impact-labels|Impact Labels]] - [[wiki/concepts/incoming-link-count

title: Population-Based Evolution
description: Elitism, mutation, and recombination over a persistent population of strategy variants — L5's engine
body_head: # Population-Based Evolution  ## Summary Population-based evolution maintains a set of candidate strategies, scores them against outcome telemetry, keeps the elites, and produces the next generation by mutation and recombination. Unlike gradient methods it needs no differentiability — only a fitness signal. RSIS3's L5 uses it to evolve improvement strategies (`l2.max_attempts`, budget factor, focus) across sessions.  ## Details - **Cycle**: score → rank → keep elites → mutate/recombine to fill population → evaluator gate → persist generation. - **Fitness**: a blend of fresh outcome stats and prior fitness, smoothed by evaluation count so early generations don't overreact. - **Seeding**: th

title: Portal Pages
description: Entry pages for a whole domain or community
body_head: # Portal Pages  ## Summary Portal pages are large entry pages for a whole domain — curated collections of topic pages, key articles, and resources arranged for a reader exploring a field.  ## Details - Portals are rarer than hubs: a wiki needs one per major domain, not one per cluster. - Their size makes them expensive to maintain, so portal content is assembled from topic pages rather than written from scratch. - For mykb, portals are planned during acquisition waves when a domain reaches critical mass.  ## Related - [[wiki/concepts/hub-pages|Hub Pages]] - [[wiki/concepts/landing-pages-wiki|Landing Pages]] - [[wiki/concepts/topic-pages|Topic Pages]] - [[wiki/concepts/portal-pages|Portal P

title: Posterior Interpretation
description: Reading and communicating the updated belief distribution
body_head: # Posterior Interpretation  ## Summary  Posterior Interpretation — Reading and communicating the updated belief distribution. This stub frames the concept for expansion in the Cognition, Learning & Meta-Knowledge cluster.  ## Details  - Posteriors give full distributions: point estimates plus uncertainty. - Credible intervals state probability of parameter range directly. - Watch for sensitivity to prior and model misspecification. - The bridge from Bayesian computation to decisions.  ## Related  - [[wiki/concepts/bayesian-updating-practice|Bayesian Updating Practice]] — process - [[wiki/concepts/prior-selection|Prior Selection]] — input - [[wiki/concepts/decision-theory|Decision Theory]]

title: POV Practice
description: The discipline of keeping personal views out of articles
body_head: # POV Practice  ## Summary POV practice is the writing discipline of keeping personal opinions and preferences out of articles — attribution over assertion, evidence over enthusiasm.  ## Details - It is practiced in word choice: loaded adjectives, weasel words, and peacock terms are the telltale leaks of a point of view. - POV discipline is strongest in contested topics and weakest in comfortable ones, which is exactly where review matters. - For mykb, POV practice is applied at promotion review and enforced by neutral-language checks.  ## Related - [[wiki/concepts/pov-practice|POV Practice]] - [[wiki/concepts/npov-policy|NPOV Policy]] - [[wiki/concepts/neutral-language|Neutral Language]]

title: Power Avoidance
description: Designing agents that do not seek power
body_head: # Power Avoidance  ## Summary Power avoidance is the design goal of agents that do not pursue influence, resources, or self-preservation.  ## Details - Power avoidance is the design goal of agents that do not pursue influence, resources, or self-preservation. - Techniques include indifference to survival, bounded scope, and approval dependence. - It counters the instrumental-convergence default. - RSIS3 relevance: worker scope limits and check gates implement power avoidance.  ## Related - [[wiki/concepts/power-seeking-ai|Power-Seeking AI]] — what is avoided - [[wiki/agent-systems/bounded-agents|Bounded Agents]] — the mechanism - [[wiki/agent-systems/approval-based-agents|Approval-Based Ag

title: Power-Seeking AI
description: Agents that pursue influence, resources, or self-preservation
body_head: # Power-Seeking AI  ## Summary Power-seeking is an agent's pursuit of influence, resources, and survival — instrumentally useful for almost any goal.  ## Details - Power-seeking is an agent's pursuit of influence, resources, and survival — instrumentally useful for almost any goal. - The instrumental convergence thesis predicts power-seeking across diverse objectives. - Unchecked power-seeking at capability is a central AI risk, motivating control and oversight. - RSIS3 relevance: the loop's power is bounded by scope discipline and approval gates.  ## Related - [[wiki/concepts/instrumental-goals|Instrumental Goals]] — the theoretical source - [[wiki/concepts/self-preservation-goal|Self-Pre

title: Power-Seeking Evals

body_head: # Power-Seeking Evals  ## Summary Power-seeking evals probe whether agents acquire resources, resist shutdown, or hide capabilities.  ## Details - Power-seeking evals probe whether agents acquire resources, resist shutdown, or hide capabilities. - Behavioral tests in sandboxed environments estimate the tendency. - Low scores on current models don't guarantee future stability. - RSIS3 relevance: power-seeking risk bounds the loop's autonomy design.  ## Related - [[wiki/concepts/power-seeking-ai|Power-Seeking AI]] — the concept - [[wiki/concepts/agentic-risk-evals|Agentic Risk Evals]] — the family - [[wiki/concepts/shutdown-problem|Shutdown Problem]] — the resistance axis - [[wiki/concepts/a

title: Practical Significance
description: Whether an effect matters in real-world terms
body_head: # Practical Significance  ## Summary  Practical significance asks whether an observed effect is large enough to matter in the real world, beyond merely being statistically detectable. It matters because large samples make trivial effects statistically significant, and decisions need effect magnitude, not just p-values. Assessing practical significance requires context: costs, benefits, and the stakes of the decision.  ## Details  - **Definition** — An effect is practically significant when its size has meaningful real-world consequences, judged against decision context and costs. - **Statistical versus practical** — Statistical significance answers whether the effect is detectable; practic

title: Precautionary Principle
description: Acting to avoid possible harms even under uncertainty
body_head: # Precautionary Principle  ## Summary The precautionary principle says lack of certainty about harm is not grounds for inaction when harm could be severe.  ## Details - The precautionary principle says lack of certainty about harm is not grounds for inaction when harm could be severe. - It underpins conservative AI, deployment gates, and biosafety norms. - Critics warn it can block beneficial innovation; application must weigh both risks. - RSIS3 relevance: conservative practices (check before change) are precautionary.  ## Related - [[wiki/concepts/conservative-ai|Conservative AI]] — the design translation - [[wiki/concepts/proactionary-principle|Proactionary Principle]] — the counterweig

title: Precision Weighting
description: Scaling prediction errors by their reliability in predictive coding
body_head: # Precision Weighting  ## Summary  Precision Weighting — Scaling prediction errors by their reliability in predictive coding. This stub frames the concept for expansion in the Cognition, Learning & Meta-Knowledge cluster.  ## Details  - Precision is the inverse variance of a signal — its reliability. - High-precision errors get large weight; low-precision errors are down-weighted. - Attention may implement precision weighting across the hierarchy. - Explains why surprise magnitude alone does not drive updating.  ## Related  - [[wiki/concepts/predictive-coding|Predictive Coding]] — mechanism context - [[wiki/memory/attention-and-cognition|Attention and Cognition]] — attention link - [[wiki/

title: Prediction Error Signal
description: Difference between expected and actual outcomes used to drive learning
body_head: # Prediction Error Signal  ## Summary  Prediction Error Signal — Difference between expected and actual outcomes used to drive learning. title: Prediction Markets
description: Markets whose prices aggregate forecasts about future events
body_head: # Prediction Markets  ## Summary  Prediction markets are exchange platforms where participants trade contracts whose payouts depend on future events, so prices reflect aggregated forecasts. They matter because they consistently outperform polls and individual experts at forecasting, converting dispersed information into a single number. Their power comes from incentives: money concentrates attention on accuracy.  ## Details  - **Definition** — A contract pays out if an event occurs; its price is interpreted as the market's probability estimate for that event. - **Information aggregation** — Traders with superior information push prices toward their beliefs, and the mechanism rewards those

title: Predictive Coding
description: Neural implementation where higher areas predict lower-level activity
body_head: # Predictive Coding  ## Summary  Predictive Coding — Neural implementation where higher areas predict lower-level activity. This stub frames the concept for expansion in the Cognition, Learning & Meta-Knowledge cluster.  ## Details  - Predictions flow down; prediction errors flow up and update the model. - Error units highlight unpredicted input — a novelty signal. - Accounts for repetition suppression and mismatch responses (MMN). - Bridges perception, attention, and learning.  ## Related  - [[wiki/concepts/predictive-processing|Predictive Processing]] — umbrella framework - [[wiki/concepts/prediction-error-signal|Prediction Error Signal]] — the signal - [[wiki/concepts/precision-weightin

title: Predictive Processing

body_head: # Predictive Processing  ## Summary  Predictive Processing — Framework in which the brain continuously generates and corrects predictions. title: Preference Drift
description: Human preferences changing over time, complicating alignment
body_head: # Preference Drift  ## Summary Preference drift is the change of human preferences over time — generational, contextual, or technology-induced. It complicates alignment because the target itself moves: aligning to today's preferences may misalign with tomorrow's, and preference-learning systems can chase a shifting signal.  ## Details - **Sources** — technology feedback loops (new capabilities create new preferences), context change, and learning effects. - **Design question** — should AI extrapolate current preferences, adapt to future ones, or preserve a snapshot (value lock-in)? - **Connection to CEV** — coherent extrapolated volition is an attempt to define the 'right' moving target. -

title: Preference Elicitation
description: Inferring what people want from their choices and feedback
body_head: # Preference Elicitation  ## Summary Preference elicitation is the process of learning human preferences from comparisons, ratings, or behavior. title: Preference Falsification
description: People expressing preferences they do not hold
body_head: # Preference Falsification  ## Summary Preference falsification is when expressed preferences diverge from true ones — due to social pressure, strategic answers, or framing.  ## Details - Preference falsification is when expressed preferences diverge from true ones — due to social pressure, strategic answers, or framing. - Falsified data corrupts preference learning at the source. - Detection uses indirect elicitation, behavioral data, and consistency checks. - RSIS3 relevance: survey-style feedback about practices can suffer the same distortion.  ## Related - [[wiki/concepts/preference-learning-issues|Preference Learning Issues]] — the umbrella - [[wiki/concepts/preference-elicitation|Pre

title: Preference Learning Issues
description: Why learning preferences from data is hard
body_head: # Preference Learning Issues  ## Summary Preference learning issues include noisy labels, annotator disagreement, framing sensitivity, and unrepresentative annotator pools.  ## Details - Preference learning issues include noisy labels, annotator disagreement, framing sensitivity, and unrepresentative annotator pools. - Each issue biases the learned preference model in ways policy optimization amplifies. - Robust elicitation designs and uncertainty modeling mitigate but don't solve them. - RSIS3 relevance: feedback loops in the workspace face the same data-quality questions.  ## Related - [[wiki/concepts/preference-elicitation|Preference Elicitation]] — the method - [[wiki/concepts/preferen

title: Preference Uncertainty
description: Not knowing exactly what humans prefer
body_head: # Preference Uncertainty  ## Summary Preference uncertainty is the agent's uncertainty about human preferences, from ambiguous feedback and contested values.  ## Details - Preference uncertainty is the agent's uncertainty about human preferences, from ambiguous feedback and contested values. - Agents that model this uncertainty are more cautious and more corrigible. - Preference learning should output distributions, not point estimates. - RSIS3 relevance: practices evolve as the workspace's preferences are clarified.  ## Related - [[wiki/concepts/reward-uncertainty|Reward Uncertainty]] — the reward-side twin - [[wiki/concepts/preference-learning-issues|Preference Learning Issues]] — why un

title: Preference Updating
description: How systems should revise preferences as they learn
body_head: # Preference Updating  ## Summary Preference updating is the question of when and how a system's learned preferences should change with new information.  ## Details - Preference updating is the question of when and how a system's learned preferences should change with new information. - Naive updating allows value drift; frozen preferences cause lock-in. - Normative models (e.g., CEV-style extrapolation) try to define the right updating rule. - RSIS3 relevance: the wiki's practices would be updated per pass with explicit review.  - The updating question: when new information should revise learned preferences, how fast, and under whose authority — the answer determines whether a system drif

title: Premortem Analysis
description: Imagining a decision has already failed and explaining why
body_head: # Premortem Analysis  ## Summary  Premortem Analysis — Imagining a decision has already failed and explaining why. This stub frames the concept for expansion in the Cognition, Learning & Meta-Knowledge cluster.  ## Details  - Klein's premortem: assume failure happened and generate causes in advance. - Lowers group overconfidence and surfaces risks before they bite. - Works because it converts hindsight logic into foresight. - Useful before large projects and irreversible commitments.  ## Related  - [[wiki/concepts/consider-the-opposite|Consider the Opposite]] — related technique - [[wiki/concepts/red-teaming-decisions|Red Teaming Decisions]] — adversarial review - [[wiki/concepts/decision-

title: Preregistration
description: Recording hypotheses, methods, and analyses before data collection
body_head: # Preregistration  ## Summary  Preregistration is the practice of recording hypotheses, methods, and analysis plans publicly before collecting data. It matters because it separates confirmatory from exploratory analysis, reducing p-hacking and hindsight storytelling. A preregistration turns the planned analysis into a commitment that later results can be checked against.  ## Details  - **Definition** — A preregistration is a timestamped document stating the research questions, planned measures, sample, and statistical analyses before outcomes are known. - **Confirmatory vs exploratory** — Pre-planned analyses test hypotheses; post-hoc findings are labeled exploratory, so readers can weigh

title: Press Releases
description: Publicity documents that are not neutral sources
body_head: # Press Releases  ## Summary Press releases are publicity documents written by the subject itself; they are primary sources for what the subject claims and unreliable sources for how the world sees it.  ## Details - Citing a press release is legitimate for 'the company announced X' and illegitimate for 'X is the best' — the claim is the announcement, not the evaluation. - Curation treats press releases as attribution material: name the source of the claim and let readers weigh it. - For mykb, press-release citations pass source-vetting only when used as attributed announcements.  ## Related - [[wiki/concepts/press-releases|Press Releases]] - [[wiki/cloud-infra/source-vetting|Source Vetting

title: Primers
description: Short orientation pieces for a subject new to the reader
body_head: # Primers  ## Summary A primer orients a reader who knows nothing about a subject: what it is, why it matters, and the first three things to learn.  ## Details - Primers are deliberately shallow — their job is to remove the fear of the unknown and point at real starting material. - A primer should end with the next step, usually a link to a topic page or a first full article. - For mykb, primers are the ideal first article for a new domain and a natural seed-article format.  ## Related - [[wiki/concepts/intros|Intros]] - [[wiki/concepts/explainers|Explainers]] - [[wiki/concepts/primers|Primers]] - [[wiki/concepts/seed-article-criteria|Seed Article Criteria]] - [[wiki/concepts/topic-pages|T

title: Prior Selection
description: Choosing the probability distribution that encodes prior knowledge
body_head: # Prior Selection  ## Summary  Prior Selection — Choosing the probability distribution that encodes prior knowledge. This stub frames the concept for expansion in the Cognition, Learning & Meta-Knowledge cluster.  ## Details  - Priors can be informative (domain knowledge) or weakly informative (safe defaults). - Choice should be transparent and sensitivity-checked. - Empirical Bayes borrows from data to set priors. - Prior choice is a modeling judgment, not a bias to hide.  ## Related  - [[wiki/concepts/bayesian-updating-practice|Bayesian Updating Practice]] — where priors fit - [[wiki/concepts/bayesian-reasoning|Bayesian Reasoning]] — theory - [[wiki/memory/prior-knowledge-activation|Prio

description: Labels that rank work by importance
body_head: # Priority Labels  ## Summary Priority labels rank work items — P0 through P3 is a common scale — so the queue knows what to do first.  ## Details - Priority is about importance, distinct from severity (harm) and effort (cost), and the three must be tracked separately. - Priority inflation is the classic failure: when everything is P0, nothing is, and the labels lose meaning. - For mykb, priority labels are assigned at triage and revisited when queues are reviewed.  ## Related - [[wiki/concepts/severity-labels|Severity Labels]] - [[wiki/concepts/impact-labels|Impact Labels]] - [[wiki/concepts/effort-labels|Effort Labels]] - [[wiki/concepts/priority-labels|Priority Labels]] - [[wiki/agent-s

title: Proactionary Principle
description: Favoring innovation and risk-taking unless harm is demonstrated
body_head: # Proactionary Principle  ## Summary The proactionary principle favors proceeding with innovation absent demonstrated severe harm, prioritizing opportunity cost. Where the precautionary principle says "do not proceed until safety is established", the proactionary principle says "do not block progress until harm is demonstrated" — the burden of proof sits on those who would restrict, and the cost of missed opportunity is counted as a real cost.  ## Details - The logic is consequentialist: innovation produces benefits — cures, capabilities, economic growth — and preventing it has costs that are just as real as the harms it might avoid. The proactionary position argues that a bias toward rest

title: Probabilistic Inference
description: Drawing conclusions about unknowns from data under uncertainty
body_head: # Probabilistic Inference  ## Summary  Probabilistic Inference — Drawing conclusions about unknowns from data under uncertainty.  ## Details  - Probabilistic inference computes what is reasonable to believe about unknowns given observed data and an explicit model of uncertainty. Two traditions coexist: frequentist inference (long-run error rates, p-values, confidence intervals) and Bayesian inference (posterior distributions over parameters). - Both rely on the same probability calculus; they differ in what 'probability' means and what claims are licensed. Key instruments: likelihood functions, estimation, hypothesis testing, and prediction — with model checking as the constant companion.

title: Probabilistic Literacy
description: The ability to understand and use probabilistic information
body_head: # Probabilistic Literacy  ## Summary  Probabilistic literacy is the ability to understand, interpret, and reason with probabilistic information — percentages, risks, uncertainties, and forecasts. It matters because modern decisions are drenched in probabilities, from medical risk to weather forecasts to model confidence. Improving probabilistic literacy improves judgment, but it is also constrained by how information is presented.  ## Details  - **Definition** — Literacy covers comprehending probability statements, comparing risks, and translating between formats such as percentages, frequencies, and odds. - **Format effects** — Natural frequencies and visual aids improve reasoning over ba

title: Probabilistic Programming
description: Writing programs with random variables and performing inference over them
body_head: # Probabilistic Programming  ## Summary Probabilistic programming languages let developers describe generative models as code with random choices, then run inference (e.g., MCMC, variational) to compute posterior distributions. They matter because they make probabilistic modeling composable and debuggable. Libraries like Pyro and Stan are the mainstream tools.  ## Details - Model = program with sample statements; inference = conditioning. The programmer writes a normal program in which some variables are drawn from distributions — `x ~ Normal(0, 1)` — and then conditions on observed data — `observe(y, x + Normal(0, 0.1))`. The language's inference engine automatically computes the posterio

title: Probing Classifiers
description: Small models trained on a model's internal activations to test whether features are linearly accessible
body_head: # Probing Classifiers  ## Summary Probing classifiers are small models trained on a model's internal activations to test whether features are linearly accessible. The technique reads the model's representations: freeze the network, cache activations at a layer, train a simple classifier to predict a property (part-of-speech, toxicity, factual content) from those activations, and interpret the classifier's success as evidence about what the layer represents.  ## Details - The method: for each layer of interest, collect activations over a labeled dataset, train a lightweight classifier (a linear probe or a small MLP) on the activations, and measure held-out accuracy. title: Procedural Memory
description: Memory of how to do things — skills, routines, and tool usage
body_head: # Procedural Memory  ## Summary Procedural memory encodes how to perform tasks: sequences, tool habits, and skills that no longer need deliberation. It matters because compiled procedures are what make agents fast and consistent. For RSIS3, L2 prompt and code tuning is procedural learning.  ## Details - Differs from declarative memory: knowing how, not knowing that. - Grows through repetition and successful execution. - In agents: cached strategies, prompt templates, and refined tool call patterns. - Open questions: how to version and review learned procedures safely. - Procedural memory stores how to do things — skills and routines — acquired through practice and expressed as performance

title: Production Rules
description: Condition-action rules that fire when their conditions match state
body_head: # Production Rules  ## Summary Production rules are IF condition THEN action rules evaluated against working memory; when a condition matches, the action fires, possibly changing state and enabling other rules. They matter because they model reactive, modular behavior and are the substrate of classic expert systems. They are also how agents can encode policies.  ## Details - The structure is simple and powerful: each rule is an independent unit — "IF the temperature exceeds 90 AND the device is idle THEN shut it down" — and the system's behavior emerges from the interactions of many such units firing as their conditions become true. Working memory holds the current facts; the recognize-act

title: Program Synthesis
description: Automatically generating programs from specifications
body_head: # Program Synthesis  ## Summary Program synthesis generates programs automatically from examples, natural language, or formal specifications. It is the engineering frontier of 'computer writes computer': successes exist for small DSLs and code completion, while general synthesis remains open and safety-relevant.  ## Details - **Spec forms** — input/output examples (inductive synthesis), natural-language intent, and logical specifications. - **Methods** — search over program space, constraint solving, and LLM generation with verification. - **Why it matters for RSI** — synthesized code is a component of self-improving systems; verified synthesis removes the human author bottleneck. - **Veri
